paragraphs: We are an integrated biopharmaceutical company committed to redefining the retina experience. AXPAXLI, also known as OTX-TKI, our investigational product candidate for retinal disease, is an axitinib intravitreal hydrogel based on our ELUTYX proprietary bioresorbable hydrogel-based formulation technology. AXPAXLI is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 registrational program for wet age-related macular degeneration, or wet AMD, which we refer to as the SOL program. AXPAXLI is currently also being evaluated in a Phase 3 registrational program for diabetic retinal disease, including non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or NPDR, which we refer to as the HELIOS program.

We also leverage the ELUTYX technology in our commercial product DEXTENZA, a corticosteroid approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, for the treatment of ocular inflammation and pain following ophthalmic surgery in adults and pediatric patients and for the treatment of ocular itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis in adults and pediatric patients aged two years or older, and in our product candidate OTX-TIC, which is a travoprost intracameral hydrogel that has completed a Phase 2 clinical trial for the treatment of open-angle glaucoma, or OAG, or ocular hypertension, or OHT. We are currently evaluating next steps for the OTX-TIC program.

DEXTENZA and our product candidates in clinical development generally incorporate therapeutic agents that have previously received regulatory approval from the FDA, including small molecules, into ELUTYX, with the goal of providing local programmed release to tailor the duration and amount of the therapeutic agent to be delivered to the eye.

The hydrogel technology that underpins ELUTYX has been used in the human body since 1992 and has demonstrated its safety and effectiveness in over five million patients across eight FDA-approved treatments since that time. Our own approved product DEXTENZA, the first and only drug-eluting intracanalicular insert approved by the FDA, has been used in nearly 750,000 eyes since launch with reported adverse events in approximately 2 of every 10,000 patients. As a result, we believe that the ELUTYX technology is well tolerated.

We believe the ELUTYX technology can provide delivery solutions for durable therapies for wet AMD, diabetic retinal disease, including NPDR, diabetic macular edema, or DME, and proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or PDR, retinal vein occlusion, or RVO, and other diseases and conditions of the eye, such as glaucoma. Our ELUTYX-based products and product candidates are hydrogels with ester bonds that are hydrolyzed over time by aqueous or vitreous humor fluid within the eye. Unlike traditional implants, the ELUTYX-based hydrogel is not rigid, does not have a shell, and does not persist following dissolution of the active drug. The factors that regulate the bioresorption of our ELUTYX polymer are temperature and pH of the aqueous environment. As body temperature and pH of the human aqueous environment are within a typical range for humans, and since water levels in the aqueous or vitreous humor are more than sufficient to saturate our polymer matrix, we believe we can program our products and product candidates so that the polymer will be intact long-enough to deliver the active pharmaceutical ingredient and then be fully bioresorbed. We believe that the ELUTYX safety profile is further supported because ELUTYX does not create an acidic microenvironment, it is easily eliminated from the eye, does not leave behind harmful byproducts, and it has soft gel properties.

AXPAXLI is seeking to address segments of the exudative retinal diseases market, which in the aggregate is estimated to include up to 8.3 million patients in the United States by 2030 and accounted for approximately $9.4 billion in U.S. annual estimated revenues in 2025, according to the Market Scope 2025 Exudative Retinal Disease Pharmaceuticals Report, published in October 2025, or the Market Scope 2025 Retina Report.

The following table summarizes the status of our key product candidates and development programs. We hold worldwide exclusive commercial rights to the core technology underlying all of our product candidates in development and have not granted commercial rights to any marketing partners other than a license agreement and collaboration with AffaMed Therapeutics Limited, or AffaMed, for the development and commercialization of DEXTENZA and OTX-TIC in certain geographies in Asia agreed to between the parties.

Our strategy is to redefine the retina experience by advancing AXPAXLI, our lead clinical asset, focusing specifically on our registrational programs for wet AMD and diabetic retinal disease, while we continue to build upon our experience in commercializing ophthalmology products. The key tactics of our strategy are:
●Advance our AXPAXLI registrational programs.

● Continue the SOL-1 Phase 3 clinical trial and expect to present 52 Week results at the 49th Macula Society Annual Meeting, taking place between February 25 – 28, 2026. All subjects have completed their Week 52 visit and have been re-dosed according to their baseline treatment assignment.

● Obtain additional clinical data from the continuation of the SOL-1 trial through the end of Week 104 and the continuation of the SOL-R Phase 3 clinical trial, for which we intend to report topline data on the primary efficacy endpoint in the first quarter of 2027, and the planned SOL-X trial, which we intend to initiate in the second quarter of 2026.
● Pending the receipt of favorable results from the SOL-1 trial and planned interactions with the FDA, we intend to submit a new drug application, or NDA, for AXPAXLI for the treatment
of wet AMD based on SOL-1 Week 52 data. We also plan to leverage the 505(b)(2) approval pathway, which could potentially shorten the NDA review timeline for AXPAXLI by up to two months.

● We plan to target a broad label in diabetic retinal disease by conducting the HELIOS registrational program in patients with moderately severe to severe NPDR and including subjects in the program who also have non-center-involved DME, or non-CI-DME, in addition to NPDR. We plan to refine our development plans and registration strategy for AXPAXLI for the treatment of diabetic retinal disease based on our anticipated discussions with the FDA regarding the regulatory pathway for AXPAXLI for the treatment of wet AMD.

paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including under the heading "Summary of Risk Factors" in this Annual Report, should be carefully considered. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we presently deem less significant may also impair our business operations. Please see the section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K captioned "Forward-Looking Statements" for a discussion of some of the forward-looking statements that are qualified by these risk factors. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects could be materially and adversely affected.

We have a history of incurring significant losses. Our net losses were $265.9 million and $193.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1,157.0 million. We have financed our operations primarily through private placements of our preferred stock, public offerings and private placements of our common stock and pre-funded warrants to purchase our common stock, borrowings under credit facilities, private placements of convertible notes, and sales of our products. We have devoted substantially all of our financial resources and efforts to research and development, including preclinical studies and clinical trials for our product candidates, including AXPAXLI and to the commercialization of DEXTENZA. Although we expect to continue to generate revenue from sales of DEXTENZA, we expect to continue to incur significant expenses and operating losses over the next several years. Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year.
We anticipate we will incur substantial expenses if and as we:

● continue our ongoing registrational programs, including the SOL registrational program of AXPAXLI for the treatment of wet age-related macular degeneration, or wet AMD, and the HELIOS registrational program of AXPAXLI for the treatment of diabetic retinal disease, including non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or NPDR;
● initiate our planned SOL-X trial, our long-term extension study of AXPAXLI for the treatment of wet AMD;
● initiate any additional clinical trials we might determine in the future to conduct for our product candidates;

Critical Accounting Policies and Significant Judgments and Estimates
paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Some of the information contained in this discussion and analysis or set forth elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including information with respect to our plans and strategy for our business, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties and should be read together with the "Risk Factors" section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a discussion of important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from the results described in or implied by the forward-looking statements contained in the following discussion and analysis.

We are an integrated biopharmaceutical company committed to redefining the retina experience. AXPAXLI, also known as OTX-TKI), our investigational product candidate for retinal disease, is an axitinib intravitreal hydrogel based

on our ELUTYX proprietary bioresorbable hydrogel-based formulation technology. AXPAXLI is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 registrational program for wet age-related macular degeneration, or wet AMD, which we refer to as the SOL program. AXPAXLI is currently also being evaluated in a Phase 3 registrational program for diabetic retinal disease, including non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or NPDR, which we refer to as the HELIOS program.

We also leverage the ELUTYX technology in our commercial product DEXTENZA, a corticosteroid approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, for the treatment of ocular inflammation and pain following ophthalmic surgery in adults and pediatric patients and for the treatment of ocular itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis in adults and pediatric patients aged two years or older, and in our product candidate OTX-TIC, which is a travoprost intracameral hydrogel that has completed a Phase 2 clinical trial for the treatment of open-angle glaucoma, or OAG, or ocular hypertension, or OHT. We are currently evaluating next steps for the OTX-TIC program.

Pending the receipt of favorable results from the SOL-1 trial and planned interactions with the FDA, we intend to submit a new drug application, or NDA, for AXPAXLI for the treatment of wet AMD based on Week 52 data from the SOL-1 trial, without necessarily waiting to receive additional clinical data from the SOL-1, SOL-R or other clinical trials. Because axitinib is FDA-approved for non-ophthalmic indications, we plan to submit an NDA under Section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, or FDCA, which has the potential to shorten the review timeline for AXPAXLI by up to two months compared to the traditional review pathway for new molecular entities.

As of February 4, 2026, the SOL-1 trial continues to maintain an exceptional rate of subject retention and per protocol-defined treatment rescues. All subjects have completed their Week 52 visit and have been re-dosed according to their baseline treatment assignment. Oversight by an independent data and safety monitoring committee has not identified any safety signals in the SOL-1 trial to date.

As of February 4, 2026, the results of the SOL-1 trial remain masked. We expect to present Week 52 results for the SOL-1 trial at the 49th Macula Society Annual Meeting, taking place between February 25 – 28, 2026.

In November 2025, we announced that the SOL-R trial has achieved its randomization target of 555 subjects. We continued to allow randomization of previously enrolled subjects that were still in the loading phase when we achieved target randomization to maintain our commitment to both patients and investigators. We completed randomization of the SOL-R trial in December 2025 with 631 subjects randomized. We expect topline data from the SOL-R trial to be available in the first quarter of 2027, an acceleration from our previous guidance of the first half of 2027.

We plan to initiate, in the second quarter of 2026, a multi-center, open-label long-term safety extension clinical trial, which we refer to as the SOL-X trial, to evaluate subjects who have completed their two-year safety follow-up visits in either the SOL-1 or SOL-R trials for an additional three years.
AXPAXLI for the treatment of diabetic retinal disease

We have initiated our registrational program for AXPAXLI for the treatment of diabetic retinal disease with the HELIOS-3 superiority clinical trial for the treatment of NPDR in November 2025. We plan to refine our development and regulatory strategy for AXPAXLI for the treatment of diabetic retinal disease based on our planned engagements with the FDA regarding the regulatory pathway for AXPAXLI for the treatment of wet AMD.

In the third quarter of 2025, we completed a pilot repeat-dose sub-study in a subset of subjects from our Phase 2 clinical trial of OTX-TIC to evaluate the safety of a repeat, sustained release dose of OTX-TIC 26 µg. OTX-TIC 26 µg was generally well tolerated after both single and repeat dosing in patients with OAG or OHT. In addition, no new safety concerns were identified following repeat-dosing of OTX-TIC 26 µg in the small subset of subjects who participated in the sub-study. We are currently evaluating next steps for the OTX-TIC program.

In October 2025, we completed an underwritten offering of 37,909,018 shares of our common stock for an offering price of $12.53 per share, or the 2025 Offering. We received net proceeds of approximately $445.6 million, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses, from the 2025 Offering.

Our net product revenue is generated from the sale of DEXTENZA to specialty distributors, or SDs, for resale to certain ambulatory surgery centers, or ASCs, certain hospital outpatient departments, or HOPDs, and certain physicians' offices, and from the direct sale by us to ASCs and physicians' offices, or Direct Sales.

paragraphs: 本公司為一整合型生物製藥公司，致力於重新定義視網膜的治療經驗。AXPAXLI，亦稱為OTX-TKI，為本公司針對視網膜疾病的 investigational product candidate，為基於本公司ELUTYX專利生物可吸收水膠基技術的阿西替尼眼內水膠。AXPAXLI目前正於一項Phase 3 登記性計畫中評估，用於治療濕性年齡相關黃斑部退化，或稱為濕性AMD，我們稱此計畫為SOL計畫。AXPAXLI目前也正於一項Phase 3 登記性計畫中評估，用於治療糖尿病性視網膜疾病，包括非增生性糖尿病視網膜症，或稱為NPDR，我們稱此計畫為HELIOS計畫。

本公司亦運用ELUTYX技術於我們的商業產品DEXTENZA，為美國食品藥物管理局，或稱FDA，核准用於治療成人及兒童患者在眼科手術後的ocular inflammation及pain，以及治療成人及年齡兩歲以上兒童患者的ocular itching，與過敏性結膜炎相關，並於我們的產品候選藥物OTX-TIC，為一種travoprost眼內水膠，已完成一項Phase 2臨牀試驗，用於治療開角型青光眼，或稱為OAG，或ocular hypertension，或稱為OHT。目前我們正在評估OTX-TIC計畫的下一步措施。
DEXTENZA與我們在臨牀開發中的產品候選藥物一般均將已獲得FDA核准的治療劑，包括小分子，整合至ELUTYX中，目標為提供局部程式化釋放，以調整治療劑在眼內的釋放時間與劑量。
支撐ELUTYX技術的水膠技術自1992年起已應用於人體，並在該時間點後的超過五百萬名患者中，於八項FDA核准的治療中，已顯示其安全性與有效性。我們核准的產品DEXTENZA，為美國食品藥物管理局核准的首個且唯一之藥物釋放眼內植入物，自上市以來已應用於近750,000隻眼睛，報告指出每10,000名患者中有約2名出現不良事件。因此，我們認為ELUTYX技術具有良好的耐受性。

我們認為ELUTYX技術可提供治療濕性AMD、糖尿病性視網膜疾病，包括NPDR、糖尿病性黃斑水腫，或稱為DME，以及增生性糖尿病視網膜症，或稱為PDR、視網膜靜脈阻塞，或稱為RVO，以及其他眼疾或症狀，如青光眼的治療方案。我們的ELUTYX基產品與產品候選藥物為具有酯鍵的水膠，會隨著時間被眼內的水性或玻璃體液體水解。與傳統植入物不同，ELUTYX基水膠不具剛性，無包覆層，且在活性藥物溶解後不會持續存在。影響我們ELUTYX聚合物生物可吸收性的因素為水性環境的溫度與pH值。由於人體溫度與人體水性環境的pH值均在正常範圍內，且水性或玻璃體液體的水量足夠以飽和我們的聚合物基質，我們相信我們可以程式化我們的產品與產品候選藥物，使聚合物在足夠長的時間內保持完整以釋放活性藥物，並在之後完全生物可吸收。我們認為ELUTYX的安全性進一步得到支持，因為ELUTYX不會造成酸性微環境，易於從眼內排除，不會留下有害副產品，且具有柔軟的凝膠特性。
AXPAXLI正試圖解決濕性視網膜疾病的市場段落，該市場整體預計在2030年時美國將包含達8.3百萬名患者，並在2025年時美國預計年收入約為9.4十億美元，根據Market Scope 2025 Exudative Retinal Disease Pharmaceuticals Report，於2025年10月發表，或稱為Market Scope 2025 Retina Report。
下表總結我們關鍵產品候選藥物與開發計畫的狀態。我們擁有所有在開發中的產品候選藥物的基礎技術的全球獨家商業權，且未將商業權授予任何行銷夥伴，除了與AffaMed Therapeutics Limited，或稱AffaMed，簽訂的授權與合作協議，用於在亞洲某些地區開發與商業化DEXTENZA與OTX-TIC。
我們的策略為透過推進我們的領先臨牀資產AXPAXLI，重新定義視網膜的治療經驗，專注於我們在濕性AMD與糖尿病性視網膜疾病的登記性計畫，同時我們持續建立在商業化眼科產品的經驗。我們策略的關鍵行動為：
● 推進我們的 AXPAXLI 登記處方程式計畫。
● 繼續進行 SOL-1 第三階段臨牀試驗，並預期在 2026 年 2 月 25 日至 28 日舉行的第 49 屆視網膜學會年會上發表 52 週的試驗結果。所有受試者已完成第 52 週的訪問，並根據其基線治療分組重新給予藥物。
● 從 SOL-1 試驗的延續至第 104 週，以及 SOL-R 第三階段臨牀試驗的延續中取得額外臨牀資料，我們預計在 2027 年第一季報告主要療效終點的初步資料，並計畫在 2026 年第二季啟動 SOL-X 試驗。
● 待收到 SOL-1 研究的有利結果及預計與 FDA 的互動後，本公司預計將提交 AXPAXLI 的新藥申請，或 NDA，用於治療濕性黃斑變性，基於 SOL-1 第 52 週的數據。本公司也計畫利用 505(b)(2) 的核准途徑，此途徑可能使 AXPAXLI 的 NDA 審查時間縮短最多兩個月。
● 本公司計畫針對糖尿病視網膜病變的廣泛標籤，透過在中度至嚴重 NPDR 患者中進行 HELIOS 登記研究計畫，並包含同時具有非中心涉入型 DME，或非-CI-DME 的受試者，除了 NPDR 之外。本公司計畫根據預期與 FDA 的討論內容，針對 AXPAXLI 用於治療濕性黃斑變性的監管途徑，來精緻化 AXPAXLI 的開發計畫與登記策略。
● 本公司計畫根據預期與 FDA 的討論內容，針對 AXPAXLI 用於治療濕性黃斑變性的監管途徑，來精緻化 AXPAXLI 的開發計畫與登記策略。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本年度10-K表報中所列之合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。部分包含於本討論與分析或本年度10-K表報其他處的資訊，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略的資訊，包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述，應與本年度10-K表報中「風險因素」部分一併閱讀，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所述或暗示之結果有重大差異的重要因素。
本公司為一整合型生物科技公司，致力於重新定義視網膜的治療體驗。AXPAXLI（亦稱為OTX-TKI），為本公司針對視網膜疾病之研發產品候選藥物，為基於我們ELUTYX專利生物可吸收水膠配方技術之軸突抑制素（axitinib）玻璃體水膠製劑。
AXPAXLI目前正於一項第三期註冊性臨牀試驗中評估，用於治療濕性年齡相關黃斑部退化症（wet AMD），我們稱此為SOL計畫。AXPAXLI目前也正於一項第三期註冊性臨牀試驗中評估，用於治療糖尿病視網膜疾病，包括非增生性糖尿病視網膜症（NPDR），我們稱此為HELIOS計畫。

我們亦運用ELUTYX技術於我們市售產品DEXTENZA，此為美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准之類固醇製劑，用於治療成人及兒童患者在眼科手術後之眼部發炎與疼痛，以及成人及年滿兩歲之兒童患者因過敏性結膜炎所引起之眼癢。我們亦於產品候選藥物OTX-TIC，為一種曲伏前列素（travoprost）眼內水膠製劑，已完成一項第二期臨牀試驗，用於治療開角型青光眼（OAG）或眼壓過高（OHT）。我們目前正評估OTX-TIC計畫的下一步措施。

待收到SOL-1試驗之有利結果及預計與FDA之互動後，我們預計將提交AXPAXLI之新藥申請（NDA），用於治療濕性年齡相關黃斑部退化症，此申請將基於SOL-1試驗之第52週數據，不一定要等待來自SOL-1、SOL-R或其他臨牀試驗的額外臨牀數據。由於軸突抑制素（axitinib）已獲得FDA核准用於非眼科適應症，我們計畫在《美國食品、藥物與化妝品法》（FDCA）第505(b)(2)條項下提交NDA，此方式可能將AXPAXLI的審查時間縮短最多兩個月，相比傳統新分子實體（new molecular entities）的審查途徑。
截至2026年2月4日，SOL-1試驗持續維持極高的受試者保留率及根據協議定義的治療救回率。所有受試者已完成第52週訪問，並根據其基線治療分組重新給藥。獨立資料與安全監測委員會對SOL-1試驗的監督至今未發現任何安全性訊號。
截至2026年2月4日，SOL-1試驗的結果仍為遮蔽狀態。我們預計將於2026年2月25日至28日舉行的第49屆視網膜學會年會上，發表SOL-1試驗的第52週結果。
2025年11月，我們宣佈SOL-R試驗已達成555名受試者的隨機化目標。我們持續允許隨機化先前已入組且仍處於負荷期的受試者，以維持對患者與研究者之承諾。我們於2025年12月完成SOL-R試驗的隨機化，總計有631名受試者隨機化。我們預計SOL-R試驗的初步數據將於2027年第一季公佈，較我們先前預期的2027年第一季提前。
我們預計於 2026 年第二季啟動一個多中心、開放標籤、長期安全性延續臨牀試驗，我們稱為 SOL-X 試驗，用以評估已完成 SOL-1 或 SOL-R 試驗兩年安全性追蹤訪視的受試者，再追蹤三年的結果。
AXPAXLI 用於治療糖尿病視網膜病變
我們已在 2025 年 11 月啟動 AXPAXLI 用於治療糖尿病視網膜病變的註冊計畫，包含用於治療非增生性視網膜病變（NPDR）的 HELIOS-3 無優勢臨牀試驗。我們預計根據與 FDA 預計的討論，針對 AXPAXLI 用於治療濕性黃斑變形（wet AMD）的監管途徑，精進 AXPAXLI 用於治療糖尿病視網膜病變的開發與監管策略。
2025 年第三季，我們完成了一項針對我們 Phase 2 臨牀試驗中部分受試者的重複劑量子研究，用以評估重複給予 OTX-TIC 26 µg 的安全性。OTX-TIC 26 µg 在單次及重複給予後，對 OAG 或 OHT 患者而言，通常耐受良好。此外，在參與子研究的少量受試者中，重複給予 OTX-TIC 26 µg 後，未發現新的安全性問題。我們目前正評估 OTX-TIC 程式下一步的行動。
2025 年 10 月，我們完成了一項有擔保的發行，發行 37,909,018 股普通股，每股發行價格為 12.53 美元，即 2025 年發行。我們從 2025 年發行中，扣除經紀佣金與其他發行費用後，獲得約 445.6 百萬美元的淨資金。
我們的淨產品收入來自於向專門經銷商（SDs）銷售 DEXTENZA 用以轉售給特定的門診手術中心（ASCs）、特定的醫院門診部門（HOPDs）以及特定的醫師診所，以及我們直接向 ASCs 和醫師診所銷售（Direct Sales）。

headings: 與我們財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金需求的依賴
我們有持續產生重大虧損的歷史。我們預期在未來數年內仍將產生虧損，並可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制我們的營運活動，或要求我們放棄對智慧財產權或產品或產品候選物的權利。
我們的重大負債可能限制現金流量，使無法投資於我們業務的持續需求，或以其他方式影響我們的營運。
我們可能無法利用我們淨營業虧損結轉及研究發展稅額抵減的大量部分。
稅法的變更或其執行與解釋的變化，可能對我們的業務與財務狀況造成不利影響。
與產品開發相關的風險
若在AXPAXLI或其他產品候選藥物的開發過程中發現嚴重不良或無法接受的副作用，我們可能需要放棄或限制這些產品候選藥物的開發。
我們可能無法成功開發基於我們專有生物可吸收水凝膠配方技術ELUTYX的其他產品與產品候選藥物。
我們已經進行，並可能在未來於美國境外的場地進行AXPAXLI及其他產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗，且美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）可能不會接受在這些地區進行的試驗資料。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，包括本年度報告表中標題為「風險因素總覽」的部分，應謹慎考量。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為較不重要，也可能影響我們的業務運作。請參閱本年度報告表表 10-K 中標題為「前瞻性陳述」的部分，以瞭解部分受這些風險因素限制的前瞻性陳述。若上述任何風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及未來成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。

我們有持續產生重大虧損的歷史。我們的淨虧損為 265.9 百萬美元及 193.5 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日所終結的會計年度。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 1,157.0 百萬美元。我們主要透過私募發行本公司優先股、公開發行及私募發行本公司普通股及預先資金權購買本公司普通股、信用融資設施下的借款、私募發行可轉換票據，以及銷售本公司產品來資金融通營運。我們已將幾乎所有財務資源與努力投入研究與開發，包括我們產品候選品的前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗，包括 AXPAXLI，以及 DEXTENZA 的商業化。雖然我們預期會持續從 DEXTENZA 的銷售中產生收入，但我們預期在接下來的幾年內仍會持續產生重大費用與營運虧損。我們的淨虧損可能在每季與每年之間大幅波動。
我們預期若並在以下情況下，將會產生重大費用：
● 繼續我們的註冊申請計畫，包括 AXPAXLI 對濕性年齡相關黃斑部退化，或稱濕性 AMD 的註冊申請計畫 SOL，以及 AXPAXLI 對糖尿病視網膜病變，包括非增生性糖尿病視網膜症，或稱 NPDR 的註冊申請計畫 HELIOS;
● 啟動我們預計的 SOL-X 試驗，為 AXPAXLI 對濕性 AMD 的長期延長研究計畫;
● 啟動我們未來可能決定進行的任何其他臨牀試驗以進行我們產品候選品的評估;
